chunks: Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi in Naysabur in the year 352 AH informed us; he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Suli informed us; he said: Ibn Dhukwan informed us; he said: I heard Ibrahim ibn al-Abbas say:

We were in the presence of al-Rida (peace be upon him) when they discussed the major sins and the belief of the Mu'tazilites regarding them: that they are not forgiven. Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Qur'an descended contradicting the belief of the Mu'tazilites,
Allah, the Mighty and High, says: 'Verily, your Lord is the Lord of forgiveness to people despite their injustice.'
The tradition is long; we have extracted from it the required passage.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the forgiveness of major sins according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) utilizes the verse 'Your Lord is indeed the Lord of forgiveness for mankind despite their injustice' (13:6) to refute the Mu'tazilite doctrine of *al-Manzila bayn al-Manzilatain*, which held that those committing major sins would remain eternally in Hell. This hadith underscores the Shia theological position that divine mercy is not restricted by the severity of the sin, affirming that major sinners are subject to God's will—either forgiven through His grace or punished temporarily before eventual entry into Paradise.
